classification.difficultyReason: Interpret height gained as the vertical opposite side and ramp distance as the hypotenuse in the supplied triangle, then select sine and evaluate.

content.prompt:
Amy walks $5.4\text{ m}$ up a ramp that is inclined at $12^\circ$ to the horizontal.

How high (correct to 2 decimal places) is she above her starting point?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5, ramp diagram below the stem
spec.description: Horizontal base, vertical right side and ascending ramp; ordinary source-blue outlines are rendered black under house style. The height remains unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: The ramp is the hypotenuse, labelled 5.4 m. Its angle to the horizontal is 12 degrees. The lower-right angle is a right angle. Coordinates derive from the supplied length and angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no height or calculated answer is printed.

answer.worked:
The height $h$ is opposite $12^\circ$, and the ramp is the hypotenuse.

$\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{O}{H}\\\sin12^\circ&=\frac{h}{5.4}\\h&=5.4\sin12^\circ\\h&\approx1.12\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
